1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif face at a comfortable size with visibly generous line spacing between paragraphs, labels and inputs.

2.why: Headings and instructions are short, sentence-case and italic-free, though the persistent Logs panel uses all-caps tokens ('TESTING ONLY', 'SIMULATION:') in small dense lines.

3.why: The single-column card layout with full-width buttons and stacked labels suits a narrow viewport, though the two-column backup-code grid and the wide log lines are the tightest elements.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Keep these codes somewhere safe. Each code works once.' and 'Scan the code or copy the setup key into your authenticator app.' are one or two short plain sentences.

5.why: Every input shows a concrete example: 'marcus@example.com', '123456' for OTP fields, 'ABCD-EFGH-IJKL' for the backup code, plus 'like 123456' in the hint text.

6.why: Each step's required reading is at most two short sentences plus a hint box; only the optional Logs panel is long, and it is not needed to proceed.

7.why: The setup key has a 'Copy setup key' button and the backup codes have 'Copy all codes', so no long secret must be typed by hand.

8.why: Step 5 displays a scannable QR code above the setup key as an explicit alternative to manual entry.

9.why: Standard labelled email and password fields are used (and step 12 shows a filled password), but the screenshots give no visible evidence of autocomplete/one-time-code attributes or password-manager integration.

10.why: A 'Step N of 5' indicator with the number highlighted sits above each card, and a single large filled blue button is the clear primary action.

11.why: Most screens ask for one thing, but the setup-options screen combines copy, hide, request-new-code and 'I added it to my app' controls, so more than one action is available at once.

12.why: The final screen plainly confirms 'Setup complete.', yet after the email-code and authenticator checks the next screen gives no on-screen success message (confirmation appears only in the technical Logs).

13.why: 'Send a new code', 'Get a new practice code', 'Hide key', 'Show setup key again' and 'Show my codes again' are all present, with explicit text 'Retries have no penalty.'

14.why: The sign-in error 'We could not sign you in. Check your email and password, then try again.' names the problem and the fix without blame, though it is not field-specific.

15.why: The interface explicitly states 'There is no rush' and 'There is no time limit for reading or retries', and no countdown, timer or auto-refreshing element appears on any screen.
